answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule: each identity's action history is scored per epoch and compared across epochs, forming a trellis of expected transitions. An identity whose transition pattern deviates beyond a threshold triggers a decaying credibility weight, so fresh identities start at the floor. A persistent low-entropy signal across epochs is required before weight rises; a single consistent epoch yields a crystal of trust too small to matter. The attacker must fund sustained, varied, cross-epoch activity for every sybil, paying full operational cost per identity.
